sections.h2: What are the options for selling quickly in Palm Coast?
sections.html: A Palm Coast owner can sell to a cash buyer, list with an agent, or sell as-is, and many homes here draw interest for canal frontage, trails and a retiree-friendly layout. This page leans on what is specific to Palm Coast and Flagler County.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Palm Coast?
sections.html:
Palm Coast is a young city on Florida's northeast coast, incorporated in 1999. The city's About page describes 70 miles of saltwater and freshwater canals, the Intracoastal Waterway, a dozen parks and more than 130 miles of connecting trails.

The city lists the St. Joe Walkway and Linear Park as Great Florida Birding and Wildlife Trails, and says visitors can spot dolphins and seabirds from Waterfront Park along the Intracoastal. Water access is what many buyers look for first, so describe it clearly. City Council meets on the first Tuesday of each month at 6:00 p.m. and the third Tuesday at 9 a.m., at City Hall, 160 Lake Avenue.

Waterfront Park covers 20 acres along the Intracoastal Waterway and is open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily, according to the city. It has a fishing pier, a floating dock, kayak and paddleboard rentals, three picnic pavilions and trail links to the wider city system, and visitors often see manatees and dolphins. The city's contact page lists Building Services at 386-986-3780 and Code Compliance at 386-986-3764, and its Departments menu includes a lien request form and a garage sale permit page, both useful to a seller clearing out a house.

sections.h2: Who lives in Palm Coast and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Growth here has been fast and retirees make up a large share of residents. The Census Bureau reports the following for the city.

sections.h2: What permits do Palm Coast homeowners need?
sections.html:
More work needs a permit than many owners assume. The city's Building Department page cites Florida Building Code section 105.1, which covers construction, alterations, repairs, re-roofs and work on electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems.

  • Pergolas, gazebos, decks, detached patio covers and greenhouses are residential accessory structures and need a permit.
  • The city uses a design wind speed of 120 miles per hour, and a pre-manufactured structure must be engineered for that figure.
  • Applications go through the online permit portal, and accessory structure review is usually done in 3 to 5 business days.
  • A permit stays active six months from issue. If it lapses without the required inspections, a new permit is required.
  • A foundation survey may be required before vertical construction.

If you added a deck or screened structure, confirm the permit was closed out. A buyer's inspector or the title company may flag the gap, and it is easier to fix before you list.

sections.h2: How does the tax calendar affect a Palm Coast seller?
sections.html:
The Flagler County Property Appraiser sets value each January 1, and the Flagler County Tax Collector bills in November. If you held title on January 1, the year's bill is yours, usually split with the buyer at closing.

  • Homestead filing closes March 1. The first $25,000 of the exemption reaches all taxes, and up to $25,000 more reduces non-school taxes on value over $50,000.
  • A paid-in-full discount of 4 percent applies in November and shrinks to 1 percent by February.
  • Non-homestead assessments cannot rise more than 10 percent a year.
  • Unpaid bills go delinquent April 1.

Ask the county property appraiser for current exemption details, since the state calendar sets only the outer dates.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Flagler County?
sections.html:
Flagler County follows the state rate of 70 cents per $100 of price in deed stamps, collected by the clerk at recording. Clerk charges come on top: $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for each added page, $1.00 per name beyond four, plus a $4 per page technology charge.

A quitclaim deed is taxable too. A Department of Revenue advisement found that a lady bird deed on the facts presented transferred no present beneficial interest and drew no stamp tax. Your closing agent will total the real figures.

sections.h2: What if the Palm Coast house is an inheritance or has an unwelcome occupant?
sections.html:
Start with the clerk's probate file. With about 29.5% of residents 65 or older, estate sales are a regular part of this market. Summary administration fits non-exempt assets of $150,000 or less, or a death over two years ago, and creditor claims are barred after the later of three months from first notice publication or thirty days from service on a required creditor.

For an occupant without permission, Florida's sheriff removal process asks for a verified complaint and conditions such as no tenancy, no family tie and no pending lawsuit. A claim of adverse possession needs seven years of possession plus tax payments and a return filed with the property appraiser, and living in a home on that claim before filing is trespass. A month-to-month tenant, by contrast, gets 30 days' notice before a monthly period ends.

faqs.q: When did Palm Coast become a city?
faqs.a: It incorporated in 1999. The city's About page calls it one of Florida's newest cities, set along canals and the Intracoastal Waterway in Flagler County.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a deck or pergola?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists pergolas, gazebos, decks and detached patio covers as accessory structures that require a permit under the Florida Building Code.

faqs.q: What wind speed does the city use?
faqs.a: 120 miles per hour. A pre-manufactured structure should be signed and sealed by a Florida licensed engineer for that speed before you buy it.

faqs.q: How long does a Palm Coast building permit stay active?
faqs.a: Six months from issue. If it expires without the required inspections, a new permit is needed.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp rate in Flagler County?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of price, collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded.
